title: Kilagen Recurring Activity Schedule
description: Validates program/schedule.yml — the recurring security activities that are not document reviews. A document's own review cycle lives in its frontmatter (last_reviewed / next_review); this file is for the work that recurs on a calendar and that no single document owns: penetration tests, DR exercises, audits, access recertification campaigns.
$comment: WHY last_completed AND NOT next_due. The next date is computed from last_completed plus frequency, so there is exactly one field to edit and it records something that happened. A hand-written next_due is a plan, and a plan that nobody updates silently becomes a lie — which is the same reason no field here mirrors a tracker's state. `tracker` is a URL to where the work is managed, never a copy of its status.

id.description: Lowercase slug, unique within the file.

frequency.description: A closed set, so the next due date can be computed rather than guessed.

owner.description: The role accountable for the activity happening. Must resolve to a role document.

last_completed.description: The date it was last actually done. The only field that normally changes.

tracker.description: Where the work is managed. A pointer, never a mirror of its state.

related.description: Document ids this activity exercises or produces evidence for.
